title: Conv2d Layers in PyTorch 🧱
description: Master `nn.Conv2d` parameters and output size calculation.

slides.title: The `nn.Conv2d` Module 📦
slides.content:
# Layer Interface

```python
conv = nn.Conv2d(in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size, stride=1, padding=0)
```

* `in_channels`: depth of input (e.g., 3 for RGB).
* `out_channels`: number of filters (depth of output).
* `kernel_size`: int or tuple.

Weights: tensor of shape `(out_channels, in_channels, kernel_h, kernel_w)`.
Bias: `(out_channels,).`

slides.title: Create a Conv Layer
slides.content: Inspect the weight shape of a 2D convolutional layer.
slides.codeSnippet:
import torch.nn as nn

conv = nn.Conv2d(in_channels=3, out_channels=16, kernel_size=3, stride=1, padding=1)
print(conv.weight.shape)  # [16, 3, 3, 3]
print(conv.bias.shape)    # [16]

slides.title: Forward Pass Through Conv2d
slides.content: Pass a mini‑batch through the convolutional layer.
slides.codeSnippet:
x = torch.randn(8, 3, 32, 32)   # batch of 8 RGB images 32x32
conv = nn.Conv2d(3, 16, 3, padding=1)
out = conv(x)
print(out.shape)   # [8, 16, 32, 32]

slides.title: Multiple Input / Output Channels 🧵
slides.content:
## Combining Filters

Each output channel is the result of a distinct filter scanning **all** input channels and summing the contributions.

Thus, the layer learns `out_channels` different feature detectors (edges, colors, textures).

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use `padding='same'` (PyTorch 1.9+)

`nn.Conv2d(3, 16, 3, padding='same')` automatically adds correct padding to keep spatial dimensions.
